title: Green Rule
concept: The one rule that can’t be broken: you can say the honest thing without being punished for it. If that isn’t true, everything else stops.
whenToUse: Always, and especially when the honest thing feels as if it will cost you, or when one of you starts threatening, shutting down or getting back at the other.
steps: Say what feels unsafe, in one sentence.
Pause the topic right away. Whoever hears it believes it first; nobody tries to prove a point.
Take a Pause + Return with an exact time to come back. If it’s fear, threats, coercion or violence, not flooding, do not return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.
When you’re back, warm up and check it feels safe again before you return to the topic.
Put it right: whoever reacted badly uses the repair line you agreed in advance, so the honest thing is easier to say next time.

phrases.text: This doesn’t feel safe right now.
Can we pause? This doesn’t feel safe.
Even if I don’t like what you say, I won’t punish you for saying it.

working: B: “I want to be honest about this, but I’m worried you’ll shut down.” A: “Thank you for saying it. I’m getting flooded. Pause 20 minutes, back at 8.10pm. I’m not leaving; I want to hear it.” B: “See you at 8.10pm.”
notWorking: A snaps, “Fine, tell me, but if it’s what I think, I don’t know why we’re together.” B’s honesty is punished, so next time it won’t get said. The rule pauses a topic; it does not cancel it.
activity: Each of you writes one sentence for when something doesn’t feel safe. Agree your default pause length. Practise once on a low-stakes honest point: one of you says it, the other only acknowledges it.
warn: The Green Rule comes before every other tool. A stated lack of safety is believed first. If you’re afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no, stop: these tools are not for this. Get outside help.
